solves.reason: Contingency implies uncertainty (not certainty), algorithms operate efficiently (not creatively), and we restore predictability (not originality).
Original text: 'not contingent', 'neither unpredictable', 'We repair'. contingent-unpredictable-repair matches.
Original: 'choose between possibilities', 'nor idiosyncratic', 'care about the moods'. possibilities-idiosyncratic-moods.
erratically contradicts the context — algorithms operate 'efficiently and reliably', not erratically.
innovative contradicts context — when a machine becomes unpredictable, we think it is 'broken', not innovative.
sluggishly contradicts context — algorithms operate 'efficiently', not sluggishly.
The dash followed by 'which is why they can operate so efficiently' indicates the cause: not being contingent. contingent fits.
Watches should indicate the same time 'if they work properly'. properly is the original word.
'We repair them precisely to restore their predictability.' precisely fits the purpose of restoring predictability.
contingent = conditional (dependent on circumstances/conditions). The passage defines contingency as implying selection and uncertainty.
idiosyncratic = peculiar (unique to an individual, distinctive). The other options are antonyms or unrelated.
restore = bring back (to return something to its previous state). eliminate and increase are different meanings.
uncertainty ↔ assurance. ambiguity and doubt are synonyms of uncertainty; complexity is a different dimension.
reliably ↔ erratically. steadily, consistently, securely are all similar to reliably.
(A) program their behavior = to code/program; (B) program workshops = to schedule/plan. Different meanings of 'program'.
A possible future event that cannot be predicted with certainty = contingency. Algorithm, instruction, perspective don't fit.
Parallel structure 'so ____ and reliably' requires an adverb. efficient → efficiently.
After 'their' a noun is needed. Context is restoring the quality of being predictable. predict → predictability (not prediction).
'designed to ____ that program their behavior' — algorithms follow instructions. The other choices contradict the passage.
'we expect algorithms to be ____' — neither unpredictable nor idiosyncratic. The passage says this explicitly. Other options contradict the argument.
